          title: City

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison

          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[-+()0-9 ]*$'

          title: Email

          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'

            Create-time flag. When true, this owner joins the shared household of any existing
            owner with the same last name and address, taking that household's householdId (which
            then forms part of its identityKey). Duplicate rejection is decided solely by the
            identityKey: only an owner whose whole identityKey equals an existing owner's is
            rejected with 409. Write-only; never returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true

        - address

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[-+()0-9 ]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address. It is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Create-time flag. When true, this owner joins the shared household of any existing
            owner with the same last name and address, taking that household's householdId (which
            then forms part of its identityKey). Duplicate rejection is decided solely by the
            identityKey: only an owner whose whole identityKey equals an existing owner's is
            rejected with 409. Write-only; never returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true

All tests pass and the build is green. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Change: optional, region-validated `postcode` on owners

The feature follows the exact pattern the codebase already uses for optional-but-validated fields (`email`/telephone): a small package-private helper called from the validate step, throwing a checked escalation that a handler turns into a 400.

**Contract (OpenAPI)** — added `postcode` to the `OwnerFields` schema (`openapi.yml`) as an optional string, so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto`/`OwnerDto` gain the field. No bean-validation pattern was added, so POST and PUT both flow through the same explicit validator and produce an identical 400 shape.

**Persistence** — added a `postcode` field/column to the `Owner` entity and a `postcode VARCHAR(4)` column to all four schemas (hsqldb — used by tests — plus h2, mysql, postgres). MapStruct maps the field by name automatically, so it round-trips through create/response with no mapper changes.

**Validation** — new `OwnerPostcode` helper:
- absent (`null`) → accepted (backward-compatible);
- present → must be exactly 4 digits, else 400;
- if the city has a known region (via the existing `Localities` table: Sydney=NSW, Melbourne=VIC, Brisbane=QLD), the value must fall in that region's range (NSW 2000–2099, VIC 3000–3099, QLD 4000–4099), else 400;
- city with no known region → any 4-digit postcode accepted.

Wired into both `ValidateOwnerFields` (POST) and `ValidateOwner` (PUT); `ApplyOwner` now copies `postcode` on update.

**Error handling** — new `InvalidPostcodeException` (checked) + `InvalidPostcodeExceptionHandler` (400, body `{"errors":["postcode"]}`) + escalation YAML, matching the existing telephone/email handlers.

**Tests** — the provided `AcceptanceTest` (stores a valid postcode, accepts an owner without one, rejects a malformed one) passes, and the full suite is green:

```
Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
BUILD SUCCESS
```

The out-of-range rejection and unknown-region-accepts-any behavior required by the spec are implemented and consistent with the pinned reference tables in the test base, even though no provided test exercises those two branches directly.
